stem:
Jatin starts factorising $84$ as $6 \times 14$ and wants a complete prime factorisation.

Which two claims correctly finish the work?

options.text: Stop at $6 \times 14$, because those factors are already named composite factors.
Continue until every remaining factor is prime: $84 = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 7$.
Choose $84$ itself as the answer, because $84$ is the largest number printed in the stem.

teacher.key_rationale: Prime factorisation continues until only primes remain: 84 = 2×2×3×7. Stopping at composites, or grabbing the printed 84, miss that test.
